description:
Hey everyone! I'm building a team to create a space mission game for this year's Space Apps Challenge. I love game design, orbital mechanics, sci-fi, and cats.

Why Join: We're focusing on a clear, achievable mechanic (a minimum viable product) that showcases real NASA data in a fun way.

Looking For: Programmers, UI/UX designers, and anyone good at storytelling or working with open NASA APIs. All skill levels welcome—let's build something awesome together!
summary:
Far from Earth, a space cat crash-lands on the unfamiliar planet EB-2484r. The cat is carrying a collection of scientific data gathered throughout its travels in the Milky Way. To bring the data safely home, the cat needs the player’s help to design a spacecraft and plan a successful mission.
Space Cat: Build a Spaceship combines a character-driven story with spacecraft design and simplified physics. Inspired by the 2D worlds of games such as Pokémon and Undertale, the game invites players to experiment, learn from setbacks, and iteratively improve their designs.
details:
Space Cat Mission: Build a Spaceship is a 2D educational game where players help a stranded space cat return home after crashing on a distant planet, EB-2484r. Along the way, players must design a spacecraft, manage limited resources, and bring home scientific discoveries collected across the Milky Way.

Players can play individually or collaborate in teams of up to four, taking on different responsibilities such as propulsion, power, communications, and budget management. The challenge is to build a spacecraft that can successfully launch and complete its mission while balancing factors like fuel, mass, energy, and cost. Every decision involves trade-offs. For example, adding a larger fuel tank might increase travel distance, but it also makes the spacecraft heavier and may require a more powerful engine.

The game introduces basic space engineering and physics concepts through hands-on experimentation rather than traditional lessons. Players can test their spacecraft, see what works or fails, receive feedback, and redesign their choices. We want players to understand that engineering isn't always about getting everything right the first time. It's about experimenting, solving problems, and learning from mistakes.

Creatively, we wanted to make space science feel more approachable and fun. Our game uses a playful pixel-art style inspired by classic 2D games like Pokémon and Undertale. Instead of presenting spacecraft engineering as a complicated technical subject, we turned it into an adventure with a cute character, a story, and interactive challenges.

Our team considered how to balance scientific concepts with enjoyable gameplay, how different spacecraft systems affect one another, and how to make the experience accessible to people who may not have a background in space science.

Ultimately, we hope Space Cat Mission encourages curiosity about space exploration, creative problem-solving, collaboration, and an interest in STEM. We want players to have fun while discovering how much thought and teamwork goes into designing a real space mission.
